report.tagline: A second-hand fashion app where young people buy and sell vintage and pre-loved clothes, now owned by eBay.
report.simpleSummary: Depop is an app for buying and selling used clothes, a bit like Instagram meets a vintage shop. Sellers post photos of their clothes, buyers scroll and follow sellers they like. Most users are under 26. It was owned by Etsy and was bought by eBay in 2026.

keyNumbers.note: eBay Q3 2026 update, up from about 9 million.

keyNumbers.note: Value Added Resource, from eBay deal disclosures.

keyNumbers.note: eBay purchase from Etsy, closed 30 July 2026. Etsy paid about $1.6 billion in 2021.

overview.whatItDoes: Depop lets anyone sell used or vintage clothes from their phone. Buyers discover items through a feed and search, and sellers build a following like a small online shop. It makes money from buyer fees, payment fees and paid boosts.
howItWorks: Sellers snap photos, add a description and price, and post.
Buyers scroll a feed, search by brand or style, and follow sellers.
Buyers pay through Depop Payments, which holds the money and protects buyers.
In the UK, sellers pay no selling fee since 2024; buyers pay a buyer protection fee instead.
In the US, new sellers pay no selling fee but pay payment processing of about 3.3% plus $0.45.
Sellers can pay to 'Boost' listings for more visibility, paying a fee only when a boosted item sells.
overview.valueProposition: Unique, affordable, eco-friendly fashion, and an easy way to make money from clothes you no longer wear.

coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Builds habit and loyalty, like Instagram.

steps.detail: Sees a Depop find on TikTok.
Downloads the app and sets style preferences.
Scrolls the feed and searches for a vintage jacket.
Makes an offer to the seller.
Pays through Depop Payments with buyer fee.
Gets the jacket and leaves a review.
Accepts and ships with a label.

businessModel.summary: Depop makes money from buyer protection fees, payment processing and boosts. After removing seller fees in the UK and for new US sellers, more of its income comes from buyers and paid promotion. It still loses money.

revenueStreams.detail: A fee buyers pay on each UK order.
Sellers pay a fee when boosted items sell.

businessModel.pricing: UK: free to sell; buyers pay a buyer protection fee. US: no selling fee for new listings since 2024, payment processing about 3.3% plus $0.45. Boost fee about 8% when a boosted item sells.
costDrivers: Marketing to win buyers and sellers
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a £25 UK sale, the buyer might pay about £1 to £2 in buyer protection fee. Depop also gets money from boosted listings. Payment costs take some of this. With an operating loss of about $109 million on $187 million revenue in 2025, Depop loses money per order after marketing and staff. eBay hopes to cut costs and add buyers through cross-listing.

howTheyGetUsers: TikTok and Instagram content from sellers
Word of mouth among Gen Z
eBay cross-promotion, such as testing Depop listings in eBay search
growth.moat: Depop has a strong brand with Gen Z and a community feel. Its sellers build followings that are hard to move. But Vinted competes on price, so the moat is mainly brand and culture.

children.description: From TikTok and Instagram content, and now from Depop listings tested in eBay search.
Share of sign-ups who buy within 30 days; low rates mean the feed is not showing them their style.
Buyers who follow several sellers get a feed of new drops and come back more often.

weaknesses: Reliance on young users who switch apps quickly
risks: Vinted's growth in the UK and US
userComplaints: The UK buyer protection fee plus postage makes cheap items poor value
Fake designer and streetwear items, and sellers asking to be paid outside the app
Support is slow and scripted when a dispute goes wrong
Search is weak at finding exact sizes and styles compared with Vinted
Sellers taking days to ship, with little penalty

improvementIdeas.idea: AI listing tool from photos, using eBay's Magical Listing tech.
Verified vintage badge for trusted sellers.
Show total cost including fees upfront.
Cross-list to eBay with one tap.

pmLessons: Community and culture can be a product's core value, not just features.
Shifting fees from sellers to buyers can grow supply, but must be clear to buyers.
Being bought by a bigger company brings resources but risks losing what made the product special.
Growth without a path to profit is risky; Depop still loses money.

interviewQuestions.question: How should Depop compete with Vinted, which is bigger and cheaper?
interviewQuestions.hint: Do not fight on price. Depop's edge is style, vintage curation and a social feed for under-26s. Pick that segment, propose two features that deepen it, and measure repeat purchase and seller retention.

interviewQuestions.question: eBay paid about $1.4 billion for a business losing about $109 million a year. What should eBay do with Depop?
interviewQuestions.hint: Share the tech underneath (payments, Magical Listing, shipping) but keep the brand and feed separate. Name the risk of losing Gen Z if it starts to feel like eBay, and set a path-to-profit metric.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce scams on Depop?
interviewQuestions.hint: List scam types: fake items, buyers claiming non-delivery, off-app payment requests. Suggest verification and payment holds for new accounts, and track fraud rate with conversion as a guardrail.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature that helps casual sellers sell faster.
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick the biggest blocker: pricing, photos or visibility. Ideas: sold-price suggestions, AI listing from photos, a free first boost. Measure median days to sale.

interviewQuestions.question: Was removing UK seller fees a good idea?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare more listings against a higher price for buyers. Rough out the revenue effect, then say how you would test it by market or seller type before going further.

When costs from normal business are higher than revenue.

Numbers that must not get worse while a team pushes its main goal.
Something that makes a business hard for rivals to copy.
